name: madvise
synopsis: int madvise(void *addr, size_t length, int advice);
description: The madvise() system call provides advice to the kernel about how a specified memory range will be used, to optimize performance. It operates on page-aligned addresses and requires the length to be rounded up to a multiple of the page size. This advice can influence caching and read-ahead strategies but does not change the application's semantics except for certain values like MADV_DONTNEED.

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: Starting address of the memory range; must be page-aligned.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Size of the memory range; rounded up to a multiple of the page size.

parameters.name: advice
parameters.description: Advice value indicating expected memory access patterns, such as MADV_NORMAL or MADV_RANDOM.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: advice is MADV_REMOVE, but the specified address range is not a shared writable mapping.
